//TR: Bu checkpoint Founder'ın 2026-10-02 'gerçek kendini kurtaran sürekli yürütme' talebini kaydeder: bağımsız UASCO-Supervisor-Watchdog görevi, 2. nesil iş koruyan kararlı giriş ve güvenli anda yükselten bootstrap. Düzlem kodu (her alt süreç için zaman aşımı, RETRYABLE_STALL) LV2'ye bırakılmıştır ve açıkça belirtilir; CLEAN iddiası yoktur.
founderDirective: Founder request 2026-10-02: harden UASCO for true self-recovering continuous execution: two-layer supervision with an independent UASCO-Supervisor-Watchdog task that does not share the worker lease; an atomic, frequently refreshed SUPERVISOR_HEARTBEAT.json; stale and progress detection with automatic recovery; timeout contracts for every child; a work-conserving scheduler that never sleeps with eligible work; bounded waits with wake fields; watchdog recovery without duplicate commit/review/merge/signing; quota is not a crash; a progress watchdog; real tests; WATCHDOG_STATUS.json fields; no Founder action for routine recovery. Implement, test, commit, review and activate; do not merely document.

founderAuthorization.rule: Explicit Founder request of 2026-10-02 to implement, test, commit, review and activate the liveness-hardening package; the protected installed-layer files strictly necessary for it are authorized (the same files BS1 introduced, plus the new liveness library, watchdog, its wrapper and selftest, which are added to the protected paths); every change keeps or strengthens trust: no elevation, no stored password, no S4U or startup trigger, fixed task names only, the watchdog never takes the worker lock or lease and never writes the transition log, the dead lease is released only under the single-worker lock with a verified hash-chained log, Global Stop stops every recovery.
founderAuthorization.constraint: installed-layer host setup only, activated by the reviewed upgrade bootstrap run once by the Founder; no change to Windows services or security settings, no credential access, no push; control-plane code (engine, executors, contracts, daemon, brokers) is not changed and arrives only through governed merges (LV2)
protectedFilesAsOriginallyRecorded: config/liveness-policy.json (new, under the protected config/ prefix)

f10Authorization.scope: exact re-application of the f9-reviewed diff ef0f3bb..550bb16; protected files limited to protectedFiles; recorded before any protected change of this package

design.twoLayers: UASCO-Autonomous-Supervisor (stable entry generation 2) and the independent UASCO-Supervisor-Watchdog task (windowless wscript wrapper, every 5 minutes and at logon, IgnoreNew, 15-minute limit, own lock watchdog\watchdog.lock and state watchdog\WATCHDOG_STATE.json; never the single-worker lock, the lease or the transition log)
design.heartbeat: .ai/runtime/SUPERVISOR_HEARTBEAT.json (+ control-root mirror) written atomically by a worker thread every 20 s and within 50 ms of every field change; main-thread shared-memory beat every 5 s; declared budgets for synchronous sections (TRUST_ROOT 600 s, PLANE_LIBRARY 300 s, UPGRADE 7200 s, LEASE_RECOVERY 300 s, PROCESS_LIST 120 s)
design.workConservingLoop: planNext (pure): eligible work + progress -> next tick at once (24 then a 30 s pause); eligible without progress -> RECOVERING with backoff 60 s doubling to 15 min; LEASE_HELD -> dead-lease release then retry; nothing eligible -> WAITING/SLEEPING until the earliest real wake time (notBefore/retryAfter, holds excluded) capped at 15 min, at least 30 s; early wake within 30 s on a durable-state change that makes work eligible or on Global Stop; LOOP_PLAN events
design.deadLease: released only under the single-worker lock with a verified hash-chained log (LEASE_RELEASED_DEAD_WORKER), at entry start and after LEASE_HELD or a killed tick
design.actionBackstop: awake-time per in-flight action of the running tick only (REVIEW 240, MERGE 120, REMEDIATE 360, IMPLEMENT 360, PACKAGE 240, SIGN 120, PHASE0 300, AUDIT 240 min); soft limit only with no Git in the tick tree (re-checked right before the kill), hard limit 1.5x; evidence in liveness\evidence; orphan sweep (dead parent, control root as a path, created after the tick) and Git-lock reconciliation; retried every pre-launcher iteration while no worker lock exists
design.watchdogClasses: STOPPED, TASK_STATE_UNKNOWN, TASK_MISSING, SUPERVISOR_TASK_DISABLED, SUPERVISOR_BLOCKED, SUPERVISOR_NOT_RUNNING (start), SUPERVISOR_STALE (heartbeat stale, main thread over budget, or no heartbeat for 10 min; restart), WORKER_LIVELOCK (eligible work, RUNNING/RECOVERING, no progress for 480 awake minutes; clock reset by a legitimate wait), WORK_CONSERVATION_VIOLATION (SLEEPING/WAITING with eligible work on two runs), LEGIT_WAITING, HEALTHY, SUPERVISOR_STARTING
design.recovery: durable recovery record before any destructive step; stop and wait; restart kills surviving supervisor processes of this control root (verify-install/activate/status runs excluded), start kills only orphans; targets re-checked against a fresh process list by creation time; Git locks of just-killed processes removed while no Git runs; provably stale single-worker lock cleared with the entry rule; abort if the watchdog task was disabled; start and confirm a fresh heartbeat from a new process (else RECOVERY_UNCONFIRMED); storm guard 3 per hour with spacing; suspend grace; 14-minute hard deadline
design.status: WATCHDOG_STATUS.json (pre-launcher era, by the entry) keeps the pre-daemon schema and adds every liveness field; SUPERVISOR_STATUS.json always; the watchdog merges its fields over the existing document on problems, replaces a missing or non-object document, and when the document is older than the larger of 10 minutes and its own staleAfterSeconds it keeps the producer's time stamp, health and reasons and adds STATUS_DOCUMENT_STALE once; an unsupported generation-1 entry is not a failure (health UNKNOWN, supervisorHealth ENTRY_GENERATION_UNSUPPORTED when the watchdog writes the document); watchdog crashes, failed runs, refused locks (exit code 75) and the hard deadline are appended to watchdog/watchdog-events.jsonl
design.twoWay: the entry starts a watchdog whose last run is older than 20 awake minutes when its task exists, is enabled and is not running; never enables a disabled one
design.delegation: ENTRY_GENERATION 2; delegation only to a plane entry of the same or a newer generation
design.bootstrap: one bootstrap per control root (named mutex, BOOTSTRAP_ALREADY_RUNNING); when the supervisor task exists (upgrade or repair): an owned upgrade marker (bootstrap PID and start time) is written, a running old watchdog instance is stopped and its processes ended (the watchdog task stays enabled), the marker is written again; launcher plane -> UPGRADE_LAUNCHER_PLANE_UNSUPPORTED at once; safe-point wait (also with only orphan supervisor processes); supervisor task disabled during file replacement, then stopped; re-check of workers and in-flight actions on one process list right before ending leftovers; Global Stop and marker ownership re-checked (UPGRADE_MARKER_LOST); five runtime files staged and blob-verified (entry last); activation skipped when already active and refused if a supervisor process appeared; marker ownership checked again, supervisor task registered, watchdog registered enabled with its first periodic run in 20 minutes; the marker is removed before the first run; the watchdog is started and confirmed after the supervisor's first-run verdict; every exit path re-enables a task the bootstrap disabled and deletes only its own marker (finally)

tests.livenessSelftest: scripts/liveness-selftest.mjs: 22 scenarios (11 with real supervisor-stub processes under an injected task controller in TEMP; pure tables; real backstop with a Git-named child; dead lease on a real hash-chained state; upgrade marker states including PID reuse and the marker identity check; prompt heartbeat write of a field change; bootstrap safe-point function extracted from the PowerShell AST); about 70-90 s
tests.bootstrapSelftest: scripts/bootstrap-autonomy-selftest.mjs: 20 scenarios in 8 parallel groups, including entry-generation-2-liveness-heartbeat-work-conserving-loop-dead-lease-and-single-instance (heartbeat and status sampled during WAITING and RECOVERING, stale watchdog started through an injected controller, second entry refused) and LV1 checks in the static, install, command-line and delegation scenarios

hostEvidence.taskRegistrationProbe: TASK_REGISTRATION_PROBE SUPERVISOR: PASS removed=True; TASK_REGISTRATION_PROBE WATCHDOG: PASS removed=True (real Task Scheduler on the Founder machine: uniquely named disabled tasks built by the production builders, registered, read back, compared, removed)

adversarialReview.workflow: four independent read-only reviewers (watchdog safety, entry runtime, bootstrap upgrade, test validity) on the uncommitted package; each refuted candidates against the code before reporting
confirmedAndFixed: HIGH (tests) end-to-end heartbeat/status checks were presence-only -> values sampled during WAITING and RECOVERING

HIGH false WORKER_LIVELOCK after a long legitimate wait (clock keyed only on the progress id) -> clock runs only with eligible work in RUNNING/RECOVERING and is reset otherwise; tested (wait then work; RECOVERING; progressing worker)
HIGH (bootstrap) a disabled watchdog could stay disabled after Ctrl+C or an exception -> finally block restores; watchdog registered enabled with a delayed first periodic run
MEDIUM supervisor's own trigger could start an entry while files were replaced -> supervisor task disabled during the install window
MEDIUM leftover kill could hit an orphan tick with an in-flight action -> safe-point wait also when only supervisor processes remain, re-check right before the kill
MEDIUM Git locks of just-killed processes kept (age rule) -> notAfter rule; retried every iteration
MEDIUM command-line process matching too broad -> path boundary, control root only for orphans, verify-install/activate/status excluded, start mode kills only orphans
MEDIUM running watchdog could race the upgrade -> bootstrap stops it and ends its processes; watchdog aborts when its task is disabled
MEDIUM backstop could kill a fresh tick on a stale marker of a killed tick -> only markers of the running tick count
MEDIUM restart verification, supervisor-tree kill and stale-lock clear untested -> tests added
LOW PID reuse in kills -> targeted kills re-checked by creation time against a fresh list
LOW durable storm-guard record and hard deadline -> recovery recorded before destructive steps; 14-minute deadline; taskkill timeouts
LOW WATCHDOG_STATUS schema replaced by the watchdog -> merge keeping schema and passive fields
LOW lastFailure overwritten, BROKEN exit status shown HEALTHY, fixed 600 s freshness -> fixed
LOW instance-lock stale removal race -> compare-and-delete
LOW watchdog confirmation window, first-run record overwrite, Global Stop during the wait, pre-tick phase accepted as safe -> fixed
LOW a tree kill after the child exited -> exit guard; soft kill re-checks Git
docs overclaims (launcher mode, wall-clock heartbeat age, early wake latency, scenario counts) -> corrected; per-child kill tests and a launcher-aware upgrade safe point disclosed under LV2

MEDIUM (found by the bundle-freeze validation under load) a reader could see a half-written heartbeat when the worker fell back to copying after a rename blocked by an open reader, leaving heartbeatAge empty in the status -> the worker retries the rename before copying and readers re-read a file that is being replaced (readJsonSettled); stress-tested with three parallel end-to-end runs plus the liveness selftest

MEDIUM (found by the second bundle freeze: the canonical tests step exceeded its fixed 600 s limit under about 4.4 of 8 cores of unrelated background load; the bootstrap selftest file took 598 s) -> fewer CIM process listings per recovery (1-2 instead of 5) and per post-kill sweep (1 instead of 2-3), blocked stubs no longer spin a CPU core (Atomics.wait), the test policy suspend-grace interval no longer misfires under slow runs, and the generation-2 end-to-end scenario uses two worlds instead of three
residual: two starters that both find the same stale instance lock at the same instant can both run (single-worker lock still prevents two ticks)
descendants are killed milliseconds after their root; a reused PID in that window is theoretically possible
in START mode a supervisor that a trigger starts during recovery is left alone; only orphans are swept
a BROKEN exit in a later iteration is reflected in the status only through the BLOCKED phase mapping (no dedicated end-to-end test)

fixes: MEDIUM Git-lock check used a process list taken before the kills (a Git process started in between could lose its lock) -> after any kill a fresh unfiltered listing taken after the kill time stamp; without kills only the 2-minute age rule (also in the entry sweep)

MEDIUM a daemon's stale WATCHDOG_STATUS.json could be refreshed as HEALTHY -> a write caused only by age keeps the producer's time stamp, health and reasons and adds STATUS_DOCUMENT_STALE and a watchdog block

LOW a dead upgrade bootstrap could leave tasks disabled; -Upgrade could find no safe point while work stays eligible -> upgrade marker: the generation-2 entry starts no tick while it is live, the watchdog stands still while it is live and heals a supervisor task left disabled when its bootstrap died; the watchdog task is no longer disabled
LOW the LV1 watchdog would restart a healthy generation-1 entry after a BS1 bootstrap re-run -> restarts need an installed generation-2 entry (ENTRY_GENERATION_UNSUPPORTED)
LOW the bootstrap leftover kill used a second listing -> one listing for the worker check and the kill

LOW snapshots in the end-to-end scenario could pair a WAITING heartbeat with an older status, and the prompt flush was timing-dependent -> snapshots require heartbeat/status agreement and the WAITING heartbeat must follow the entry's own SLEEPING record within 5 s
LOW the killTargets list path (used in production) was untested -> tested
LOW documentation overclaims about kills, Git locks and freshness -> corrected

adversarialReview.loadReduction: the bootstrap selftest shares one fixture template across its shard processes (built once by the orchestrating process, read-only clone source); a measured attempt to split long scenarios into twelve shards made the critical shard slower on the saturated machine (492 s against 435 s) and was reverted

thirdRound.workflow: lv1-round6-verification (independent lenses on 39e5e22: marker lifecycle, fresh Git check, stale status, generation guard, tests and documentation; two skeptics per finding)
fixes: HIGH every upgrade ended in FIRST_RUN_FAILED because the marker was still live when the new entry started (it quiesced instead of ticking) -> the bootstrap removes its marker after both tasks are registered and before the first run; Resolve-FirstRunState gives no verdict for an UPGRADE_QUIESCE heartbeat; static order checks

MEDIUM a heal deleted the stale marker even when re-enabling the supervisor task failed or its state was unknown (the task stayed disabled for good) -> the marker is deleted only when the task is enabled again or was never disabled; otherwise the next run retries

MEDIUM a restart without a kill did not count the task stop as a kill for the Git-lock check (a fresh lock left by a Git process the stop ended stayed for 2 minutes, in launcher mode until the next recovery) -> notAfter is the stop time; the evidence records it
MEDIUM the relisting after a restart kill was untested -> a test-only process-list hook of the injected controller starts a control-root orphan right after the first listing; it must be swept

MEDIUM the quiesce test covered only a marker present before the entry started -> the marker is written while the entry runs; the entry quiesces at its next tick boundary, keeps its wake time ahead over two refreshes, and the bootstrap's own safe-point function accepts that heartbeat

LOW marker removal had no owner check (a heal or another bootstrap could remove a live bootstrap's marker) -> the watchdog re-reads the marker before re-enabling and before deleting (same PID and start time); the bootstrap re-writes it after stopping the watchdog, checks ownership before installing and before registering (UPGRADE_MARKER_LOST), deletes only its own marker, and runs alone per control root (named mutex, BOOTSTRAP_ALREADY_RUNNING)
LOW a reused PID kept a dead bootstrap's marker live for up to 3 hours -> the watchdog checks the PID's creation time against the marker (PID_REUSED)
LOW quiesce blocked the tick that recovers an in-flight action, so the bootstrap waited 30 minutes -> the entry quiesces only while no action is in flight
LOW on a launcher plane -upgrade waited 30 minutes for a safe point that cannot come -> it stops at once with UPGRADE_LAUNCHER_PLANE_UNSUPPORTED (a launcher-aware upgrade stays deferred to LV2)

LOW a status document that is not an object, or has no time stamp, was rewritten in a broken form; the staleness limit ignored the document's staleAfterSeconds -> a full document replaces it; the limit is the larger of 10 minutes and staleAfterSeconds
LOW a healthy generation-1 entry was reported as a failure every run -> ENTRY_GENERATION_UNSUPPORTED is not a failure and reports health UNKNOWN; a not-running generation-1 entry is started (tested)
LOW one-line mutations not caught (staleness reason repeated, Enable on an enabled task, marker written during a recovery) -> tested
LOW the WAITING promptness check depended on the sampler's timing under load -> replaced by a load-independent unit test of the heartbeat thread's prompt write
LOW documentation statements did not match the code -> corrected
thirdRound.robustness: round 7: an error of the heartbeat worker thread no longer crashes the entry (reported, logged as HEARTBEAT_THREAD_FAILED, restarted up to 3 times); uncaught exceptions are logged as ENTRY_CRASH/ENTRY_FAILED and WATCHDOG_CRASH; selftest failure messages include the entry output and event log (motivated by one unexplained entry exit at STARTING under heavy load during the 39e5e22 validation)
residual: the watchdog re-reads the marker right before re-enabling and right before deleting; a bootstrap that writes its marker in the milliseconds between that re-read and the delete loses it only until it writes the marker again after stopping the watchdog, and the upgrade continues; this call-site re-check has no deterministic test (the identity check is tested, also on a marker written by the bootstrap's own functions)
a bootstrap paused for more than 3 hours counts as dead; the resumed bootstrap stops at its next ownership check
a bootstrap that dies while files are being installed can leave new and old installed files side by side until the command is run again (the watchdog only re-enables the supervisor task)

during the first LV1 installation no watchdog exists yet: a bootstrap that dies between disabling the supervisor task and registering the tasks leaves the supervisor disabled until the command is run again

the cause of the single entry exit at STARTING under heavy load (39e5e22 validation) was not reproduced; round 7 adds survival of heartbeat-thread errors and crash records so a recurrence is diagnosable
